clue.text: Find nothing during search in valley

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the span of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone combing a valley for something and coming up empty-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' is a link word here. A COOMB (also combe) is a short steep valley, common in place names in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A coomb is a small steep-sided hollow or dale, a kind of narrow vale.

clue.text: Recollecting cry "ripe", he makes this dessert

indicators.note: re-collecting, gathering the letters together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A man recalling a shout of 'ripe' as he bakes a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollecting' is read as re-collecting, the anagram signal, over CRY, RIPE and HE; 'makes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case filled with red stone fruit is a classic baked pudding.

clue.text: Measure circle? It's set up in computer

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the computer abbreviation

parts.note: PC is a personal computer

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is raised, read bottom to top

parts.note: the word it, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: A geometry query about measuring a circle on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' works because this is a down clue, read upwards. The definition is a pub term: an optic is a bar device dispensing a measured shot of spirits, common in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic fixed to an upturned bottle delivers a fixed quantity of spirit, a pub measure.

clue.text: Fight annoyance, having blown top in a shop

parts.note: a bout is a fight or contest

indicators.note: losing the top in a down clue means the first letter goes

parts.note: pique is irritation, annoyance

explanation.surface: A customer losing their temper in a shop after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having blown top' removes P from PIQUE; 'in a' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boutique is a small fashionable store, typically selling clothes.

clue.text: One of the lower seeds has argument with crazy guy

parts.note: grounds are the basis of an argument; a ground is a reason argued
a nut is slang for a madman

explanation.surface: A low-ranked tennis seed quarrelling with a lunatic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tournament seeding; the seeds are literal, and 'lower' because a peanut ripens underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut plant buries its pods in the soil, so its kernel is a seed found lower than most.

clue.text: Try publicity as a stimulus

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
an ad is an advertisement, publicity

explanation.surface: Advice to use advertising as an incentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A goad is a spiked stick for driving cattle, and figuratively any spur or prod.

clue.text: Prepared to travel, in the main

definitions.text: Prepared to travel, in the main

parts.words: Prepared to travel, in the main
parts.note: the main is the high sea, so this describes a ship built for voyages there, not something mostly ready

explanation.surface: Someone who is mostly ready for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly'; the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship designed for crossing the open sea is fit to travel on the main.

clue.text: One's excluded from smarter gossip

indicators.note: excluded from means the letter for one is removed from the synonym

parts.note: nattier means smarter, better dressed
I is the Roman numeral one, the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A loner shut out of the smart set's chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' takes I out of NATTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chat idly at length, a British word for gossiping.

clue.text: State income we fiddled, without a vote

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram goes around the vote mark
fiddled means falsified, so the letters of income and we are jumbled

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A tax fraud in which earnings were fiddled and no vote cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' suggests tax fraud but is the anagram signal; 'without' is the old sense 'outside', so it is a container indicator, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the south-west.

clue.text: Timber frames with fine adjustment

indicators.note: frames means the timber surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: teak is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: A carpenter making delicate adjustments to wooden frames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' looks like a noun in the carpentry picture; it is the container verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a small refining change made to improve something.

clue.text: Attendants scrambled out in anger

indicators.note: in means the shuffled word is set inside the synonym for anger

parts.note: to enrage is to anger, as a verb

indicators.note: scrambled means the three letters of out are jumbled

explanation.surface: A star's retinue rushing out in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' jumbles the short word; 'anger' must be read as a verb to give its synonym, which is then split open by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of followers and staff who accompany an important person.

clue.text: Sweat out traditional punishment

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of sweat are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Sweating out a spell of old-fashioned discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: A TAWSE is a leather strap with split ends, formerly used to punish pupils in Scottish schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish leather strap was the customary instrument of school corporal punishment.

clue.text: Shrink from using about twice the fuel

parts.note: about is used twice: first as re, meaning concerning
about used a second time: c, short for circa
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Someone recoiling from a doubled fuel bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about twice' supplies two different abbreviations for 'about'; 'using' and 'the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil from something is to flinch or draw back from it in fear or disgust.

clue.text: Thoughtless reaction from madly keen fool

indicators.note: madly signals that the letters of keen are thrown wildly into a new order

parts.note: a jerk is a stupid or contemptible person

explanation.surface: An eager idiot reacting without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges KEEN to KNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex response made automatically, without any reflection, is described with this hyphenated phrase from the knee reflex test.

clue.text: I talk a lot about mad character on telly

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland
the box is British slang for television

explanation.surface: A talkative TV presenter discussing a crazy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer itself, a self-description.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is someone who never stops chatting, so the phrase is its own confession.

clue.text: Safe place to insert needle for such unusual injection in wing

indicators.note: an injection in something is put inside it, so the shuffled letters go inside the wing

parts.note: a pinion is a bird's wing

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of such appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A medical instruction about where to give an odd injection in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' is the anagram signal and 'injection in' the container; 'for' is a link word. The medical surface hides a sewing definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small padded cushion is where needles and pins are safely stuck when not in use.

clue.text: Lead's set up — one old star is open to negotiation

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is lifted and read upwards

parts.note: the van is the lead, the vanguard; the 's is a link
I is the Roman numeral one
Clark Gable, a film star of the 1930s

explanation.surface: Talk of a leading old film actor whose contract may be renegotiated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns VAN to NAV. 'Negotiation' is the sense of getting through a river or channel, not haggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that can be negotiated by boat is passable for shipping.

clue.text: Inflexible, having dismissed opening argument

indicators.note: dismissing the opening means the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: stiff means rigid or inflexible

explanation.surface: An unbending debater who threw out the opening argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dismissed opening' takes the first letter S off STIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor row between friends or partners.

clue.text: Keep very cool, and extricate last character on railway

parts.note: to free is to release, extricate
zed is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A rail traveller freeing the last passenger while staying calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep very cool' sounds like 'stay calm'; it means preserving food by freezing. 'and' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Freeze-drying preserves food by freezing it and removing moisture in a vacuum.

clue.text: Article limited? Was in plentiful supply

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
bounded means limited, restricted

explanation.surface: Asking whether a product was limited and finding there was plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition means the opposite of 'limited', which disguises the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in large numbers, to be present in great quantity.

clue.text: Yvonne's heartlessly rejected, showing resentment

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the shortened name is read in reverse
heartlessly means the middle of the name is removed

parts.note: the woman's name Yvonne, the 's being a link

explanation.surface: Poor Yvonne cruelly spurned and full of bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the central ON to leave YVNE; 'rejected' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for what someone else has; 'showing resentment' stands for it as the jealous feeling itself.

clue.text: On the rocks hard, split apart

parts.note: stony means hard, like stone
broke means split or smashed apart

explanation.surface: A rock on the shore, hard yet split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' looks like a description of a shipwreck or a drink; here it means penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the rocks is an idiom for being in financial ruin, entirely without money.

clue.text: Doctor admitting husband is in danger

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the husband goes inside

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: A doctor conceding a husband's life is at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here; 'is in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of possible harm, a menace or peril.

clue.text: Fair entertainment for a VIP

definitions.meaning: a Ferris ride at a funfair, a large rotating vertical ride

explanation.surface: A celebrity treated to an evening at the funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the giant revolving fairground ride and, informally, an influential person.

clue.text: It's instrumental in getting bishop to the top in a new job

indicators.note: to the top means the bishop letter is moved up to the start

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop promoted to the top in a new post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting bishop to the top' takes the B of A N JOB up to the front, giving B A N JO.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument, so it is literally instrumental.

clue.text: Such a glassmaker's speaking volumes

indicators.note: speaking signals the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: quarts are units of liquid volume

explanation.surface: A glassblower's chatter said to speak volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: QUARTS and the answer sound alike; 'speaking volumes' looks like an idiom but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz, pure silica, is melted to make fused glass, so it is the raw material of such a maker.

clue.text: Settle down after being in a flap?

definitions.text: Settle down after being in a flap?

parts.words: Settle down after being in a flap?
parts.note: a flap read as the flapping of wings: a bird alights for the night after flying

explanation.surface: Calming down after a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flap' means agitated, but the flap here is a bird's wingbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they settle on a perch to rest after flight.

clue.text: Time for hobby, say

definitions.meaning: a prison sentence, from rhyming slang ...-lime for time
the hobby is a small falcon, an example of a feathered creature

explanation.surface: Time set aside for a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a prison term this, and a hobby falcon is one such winged animal.

clue.text: Half-heartedly steal gold coin

indicators.note: half the heart is lost: one of the two central letters of the synonym goes

parts.note: to nobble is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A thief lukewarmly pocketing a gold piece.
explanation.walkthrough: NOBBLE has a doubled B at its heart; 'Half-heartedly' removes one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble was a medieval English gold coin first minted under Edward III.

clue.text: Learner's in difficulty with pen, lacking vision

indicators.note: in means the learner's letter is placed inside the difficulty

parts.note: a bind is a tiresome predicament
L is the learner sign on a British car
a fold is a pen for sheep

explanation.surface: A learner struggling with a pen and unable to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'pen' is an enclosure for animals, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Blindfold as an adjective means having the eyes covered and so unable to see.

clue.text: Stressed patent must get taken out

parts.note: patent means obvious, open
axed means eliminated, cut out

explanation.surface: A patent applicant stressed about one being withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks like an invention licence; it is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtaxed means strained by excessive demands, worn down beyond capacity.

clue.text: Eccentric spotted?

explanation.surface: Has that oddball been seen?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means crazy in a harmless way, and whimsically also describes something speckled.
